prompt: Here's a rate limiter that worked fine in staging against a standalone Redis instance. It enforces three nested quotas — per-user, per-tenant, and a global safety cap — in one atomic check-and-increment using a single multi-key Lua script. After promoting to production, the team switched Redis to a Redis Cluster for horizontal scale, and now every single call to `consume()` throws `CROSSSLOT Keys in request don't hash to the same slot` — no request is ever admitted. Walk me through why identical code that ran fine on standalone Redis fails on the cluster, then show me how you'd fix it so the three counters are still updated atomically. Also tell me what trade-off your fix introduces.
